title: Use matched preview observations to size eligible hosted shuffle jobs
question: Can inexpensive preview and container facts improve Auto memory selection, and does larger input justify a full Analyze before Run?
summary: Hosted Auto reuses a matching input preview to size eligible shuffles and supports a bounded gzip trailer hint. Analyze can refine that budget. The 2 GiB sorts still merged at both tested budgets, and fresh Analyze cost 15 to 29 seconds on the scale panel without changing Run.

workloads: Bundled Chromium on WSL2, file-backed 2 GiB shuffles and 4 GiB streaming with persistent OPFS.
Hosted plain and gzip uniform shuffle, skewed partition followed by shuffle, and two competing 42-column jobs.

validation.summary: Validated 12 multi-GiB jobs, the integrated memory observations, capped output, source fields, row conservation, grouping, stream order, publication and cleanup. Acceptance rejected a damaged gzip checksum despite a plausible size hint.

limitations: Single WSL2 host and a small synthetic panel. Sampled browser RSS includes shared pages and differs from working reservations.
The last gzip member reports decoded size modulo 4 GiB, and the eight-row preview can miss tail widths.
exclusions: Automatic Analyze triggers, arbitrary budget increases on large files, unrelated runtimes and new execution strategy promotion.
reopen_when: Calibrate cheap facts that identify a material Analyze plus Run saving on distinct workloads, including width skew and concatenated compressed inputs.
